questions.stem: Which Indian city is called the 'Manchester of India' owing to its century-old concentration of textile mills and cotton trade?

options.option_text: Coimbatore — referred to as the 'Manchester of South India' for its spinning mills
Ahmedabad — Gujarat's textile capital with India's oldest cloth mills since the 1860s
Ludhiana — Punjab's knitwear export hub, nicknamed 'Manchester of North India'
Surat — world's premier diamond-cutting hub; handles 90% of global rough diamond supply

questions.explanation: B is correct. Ahmedabad earned 'Manchester of India' for its massive cotton textile industry dating to the 1860s. Option A is the most PYQ-frequent trap — Coimbatore holds 'Manchester of South India' for its spinning mills, which is a real but distinct sobriquet. Option C (Ludhiana) is 'Manchester of North India' specifically for woollen knitwear exports — examiners deliberately plant all three Manchester variants as distractors.

questions.stem: The honorific 'Lokmanya' — meaning 'Accepted by the People' — was conferred on which freedom movement leader known for popularising Ganesh Chaturthi as a platform for national mass mobilisation?

options.option_text: Lala Lajpat Rai — known as 'Punjab Kesari'; led militant nationalism across Punjab
Bal Gangadhar Tilak — launched Ganesh Utsav (1893) and Shivaji Jayanti for mass unity
Bipin Chandra Pal — the 'Pal' of Lal-Bal-Pal; advocated passive resistance from Bengal
Gopal Krishna Gokhale — moderate leader who founded the Servants of India Society

questions.explanation: B is correct. Tilak was hailed 'Lokmanya' because he turned Ganesh Chaturthi (from 1893) and Shivaji Jayanti into forums for anti-British awareness among common people. Option A is the sharpest distractor — Lala Lajpat Rai carries 'Punjab Kesari', not 'Lokmanya'. Option C (Bipin Chandra Pal) was the third member of the same extremist trio but never received this specific honorific.

questions.stem: Which Indian city is nicknamed the 'Pittsburgh of India' and is notable for being Asia's first planned industrial township, established by the Tata Group in 1907?

options.option_text: Durgapur — 'Ruhr of India'; West Bengal steel corridor hosting SAIL's Durgapur plant
Bhilai — SAIL's Bhilai Steel Plant in Chhattisgarh, built with Soviet assistance in 1959
Rourkela — Odisha's steel city with the first integrated state-owned plant post-Independence
Jamshedpur — home of TISCO (now Tata Steel), Asia's first major private steel plant, est. 1907

questions.explanation: D is correct. Jamshedpur earned 'Pittsburgh of India' because TISCO — founded by Jamsetji Tata in 1907 — was Asia's first privately built integrated steel city. Option A is a deliberate high-quality trap: Durgapur has its own sobriquet 'Ruhr of India', named after Germany's industrial heartland, and candidates who half-remember a steel-themed nickname pick it. Options B and C were SAIL plants built post-Independence with foreign government aid, not Tata private enterprise.

questions.stem: The sobriquet 'Grand Old Man of India' is linked to which leader who authored the pioneering economic tract 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' and was the first Asian elected to the British Parliament?

options.option_text: Surendranath Banerjee — 'Rashtraguru'; founded the Indian Association in Calcutta, 1876
Pherozeshah Mehta — Parsi constitutionalist who co-founded the Bombay Presidency Association
Dadabhai Naoroji — Liberal MP for Finsbury (1892); formulated the 'Drain of Wealth' theory
Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee — first President of the Indian National Congress in 1885

questions.explanation: C is correct. Dadabhai Naoroji (1825–1917) earned 'Grand Old Man of India' for over five decades of public service. He proved economic exploitation through the Drain Theory and won the Finsbury seat in 1892 as a Liberal MP — the first Asian in the British Parliament. Option A (Surendranath Banerjee) is the leading distractor since he was also an elderly Congress stalwart, but his sobriquet is 'Rashtraguru', which examiners exploit as a confusion point.

questions.stem: The sobriquet 'Deshbandhu' (Friend of the Nation) belongs to which Bengali leader who, along with Motilal Nehru, co-founded the Swaraj Party in 1923 to contest elections from within the legislatures?

options.option_text: Subhas Chandra Bose — 'Netaji'; organized the INA and founded the Forward Bloc in 1939
Chittaranjan Das — Bengal's foremost barrister who defended many revolutionary nationalists
Surendranath Banerjee — 'Rashtraguru'; led Bengal partition protests from Calcutta in 1905
Bipin Chandra Pal — propagandist for Swaraj; deported for his Swadeshi movement speeches

questions.explanation: B is correct. C.R. Das earned 'Deshbandhu' for his selfless commitment — he donated his personal income, defended jailed revolutionaries pro bono, and forged the Swaraj Party to work within legislatures rather than boycott them. Option A (Netaji Bose) is the sharpest distractor: both are iconic Bengali leaders who eventually broke from mainstream Congress, but Bose came a generation later and formed the Forward Bloc (1939), not the Swaraj Party (1923).

questions.stem: Which Mughal emperor earned the sobriquet 'Zinda Pir' (Living Saint) from devout Muslim subjects for his strict personal austerity — stitching caps and copying the Quran for his own income — even as his political reign remained deeply contested?

options.option_text: Shah Jahan — remembered for the Taj Mahal and Red Fort; renowned for his opulent court
Akbar — promoted Din-i-Ilahi and is celebrated for his inclusive religious experiments
Aurangzeb — reimposed jizya and lived austerely; revered as 'Zinda Pir' by pious Muslims
Humayun — exiled to Persia; regained Delhi with Safavid military support in 1555

questions.explanation: C is correct. Aurangzeb's personal piety — rigid fasting, night prayers, earning by stitching caps, refusing luxuries from the treasury — earned him 'Zinda Pir' from orthodox Muslims. Yet the same reign reimposed jizya (1679) and destroyed the Kashi Vishwanath and Mathura temples. Option B (Akbar) is the classic paper-setter trap: students instinctively link 'religious devotion + Mughal emperor' to Akbar. But Akbar's faith was syncretic Din-i-Ilahi, rejected by orthodox Muslims — the opposite of the piety 'Zinda Pir' recognises.

questions.stem: Which Indian revolutionary earned the affectionate sobriquet 'Masterda' from his followers, organised the 1930 Chittagong Armoury Raid to seize weapons for an armed uprising, and was executed by the British in January 1934?

options.option_text: Khudiram Bose — youngest Bengali revolutionary; hanged in 1908, Muzaffarpur bomb case
Surya Sen — Chittagong schoolteacher who masterminded and led the 1930 Armoury Raid
Bhagat Singh — hanged in 1931 for the Central Legislative Assembly bombing in Delhi, 1929
Batukeshwar Dutt — co-accused with Bhagat Singh; sentenced to transportation to the Andamans

questions.explanation: B is correct. Surya Sen — a schoolteacher — was called 'Masterda' (Respected Teacher) by his cadre. His group seized the Chittagong Armoury on 18 April 1930, cut telegraph lines, and proclaimed a Provisional Revolutionary Government. He was captured after years in hiding and hanged on 12 January 1934. Option A (Khudiram Bose) is the most frequent confusion — both are young Bengali revolutionaries, but Khudiram belonged to the Anushilan Samiti era (1908), a full 22 years earlier. Option C (Bhagat Singh) operated in Punjab and Delhi, not Bengal, and his sobriquet was 'Shaheed-e-Azam'.
